slides.title: Attack Vector 2.1: Introduction to Cheat Engine
slides.heading: Dynamic Memory Scanning & Debugging Fundamentals
items: ▶ What is Cheat Engine?
An open-source memory scanner and debugger that inspects and modifies the virtual memory (RAM) of running Windows processes.
▶ Multi-Pass Value Filtering:
1. First Scan: Search TargetGame.exe RAM for the current health value (e.g., 100 HP) -> returns hundreds of candidate addresses.
2. Next Scan: Take damage in-game (e.g., 85 HP) and filter candidates until the exact health address is isolated.
▶ Limitation of Direct Value Scanning:
Heap addresses change every time the game restarts (dynamic allocation + ASLR), requiring a static pointer offset for permanent tools.

slides.title: Attack Vector 2.8: Process DACL Access Control Locking
slides.heading: Blocking OpenProcess via Windows Security Descriptors
items: • Discretionary Access Control List (DACL): Every Windows process has a security descriptor governing which users and processes can open handles to it.
• Self-Hardening via SetSecurityInfo(): At startup, TargetGame.exe modifies its own process DACL to explicitly deny PROCESS_VM_READ and PROCESS_VM_WRITE.
• Immediate Exploit Rejection: External calls to OpenProcess() fail immediately with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (Error Code 5).
• Lightweight Deployment: Requires zero kernel drivers or administrator privileges to block standard user-mode memory editors.

slides.heading: Why Internal Injected Code is Superior to External WPM
items: • Internal Execution Context: The injected DLL runs inside TargetGame.exe's own virtual address space with full process privileges.
• Zero Syscall Overhead: Reads and writes memory directly via native C++ pointers (*player = val) in <1 nanosecond instead of slow OS system calls.
• Direct Function Hooking: Can detour internal game functions (TakeDamage, Reload, OpenGL wglSwapBuffers) to build ESP overlays and aimbots.
• Four-Stage Injection Pipeline: VirtualAllocEx -> WriteProcessMemory -> CreateRemoteThread -> DllMain.

slides.title: Enterprise Defense: Kernel-Mode Callbacks (Ring 0)
slides.heading: OS Kernel Interception & Handle Stripping
items: ▶ ObRegisterCallbacks (Handle Stripping)
Intercepts OpenProcess in Ring 0 before returning to user mode. Strips PROCESS_VM_WRITE and PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD permissions so Cheat Engine and injectors fail silently.
▶ PsSetLoadImageNotifyRoutine
Fires a kernel callback on every DLL load. Verifies cryptographic code-signing certificates and blocks unsigned injected modules.
▶ PsSetCreateThreadNotifyRoutine
Monitors cross-process thread creation and blocks any remote thread starting at LoadLibraryA or unbacked memory.

slides.title: Enterprise Defense: Detecting Manual Mapping
slides.heading: Catching Stealthy Reflective / Manual-Mapped DLLs
items: ▶ The Manual Mapping Bypass
Advanced cheats avoid LoadLibraryA altogether—they allocate raw memory via VirtualAllocEx, manually resolve imports, and jump to the entry point.
▶ Kernel Memory Walk (ZwQueryVirtualMemory)
The anti-cheat driver scans all committed memory pages inside TargetGame.exe.
▶ MEM_IMAGE vs. MEM_PRIVATE
Legitimate DLLs loaded by Windows are backed by disk files (Type == MEM_IMAGE).
▶ The Smoking Gun
Any page with PAGE_EXECUTE_READ permissions and Type == MEM_PRIVATE is unbacked executable code—definitive proof of manual mapping!
